SURAH "AL-QADR" (THE DECREE)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

﴿Indeed, We sent it down during the Night of Decree.﴾ He glorified the Qur'an by ascribing its sending down to Himself alone, without anyone else, and He used a pronoun for it rather than its explicit name, since there is no need to draw attention to it. He also elevated the status of the time in which He sent it down. It is narrated that it was sent down all at once during the Night of Decree from the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz) to the lowest heaven (al-sama' al-dunya). Then Jibril used to convey it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over twenty-three years.

The meaning of "Laylat al-Qadr" is: the night of the determining and decreeing of affairs. "Al-Qadr" means "the determination" (al-taqdir). Or it was named so because of its nobility over the rest of the nights. It is the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan. Thus Abu Hanifa (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated from 'Asim, from Zirr, that Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to swear by Allah that the Night of Decree is the twenty-seventh night of Ramadan. This is also the view of the majority.

Perhaps the reason for concealing it is that whoever seeks it may devote many nights to worship, seeking to coincide with it. This is like the concealment of the Middle Prayer (al-Salat al-Wusta), the Greatest Name (ismihi al-a'zam), the time of answered supplication on Friday, His pleasure in acts of obedience, and His anger in acts of disobedience. And in a hadith: "Whoever encounters it should say: 'Allahumma innaka 'afuwwun tuhibbu al-'afwa fa'fu 'anni' (O Allah, You are Forgiving and You love forgiveness, so forgive me)."
(p-666) ﴿And what will make you know what the Night of Decree is?﴾ That is: your knowledge does not reach the utmost of its excellence. Then He explained that to him by His saying:

Verse 3: ﴿The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months.﴾ It contains no Night of Decree. The reason its virtue reaches this degree is what descends in it of the angels and the Spirit, by the permission of their Lord, concerning every matter (﴿Therein descend the angels and the Spirit by permission of their Lord, concerning every matter﴾), and the decree of every wise affair (﴿every matter, decreed with wisdom﴾).

It has been mentioned, regarding the specification of this period, that the Prophet (ﷺ) mentioned a man from the Children of Israel who wore weapons in the way of Allah for a thousand months. The believers marveled at this, and their own deeds seemed small to them, so they were given a night that is better than the duration of that warrior.

The angels descend (تَنَـزَّلُ المَلائِكَةُ), to the lowest heaven, or to the earth,

and the Spirit (والرُوحُ), that is Jibril (Gabriel), or a kind of angels whom the (other) angels do not see except on that night, or the mercy (of Allah).

﴿Therein, by the permission of their Lord, with every decree﴾. That is: they descend because of every matter (مِن أجْلِ كُلِّ أمْرٍ) which Allah has decreed for that year, until the next (year). And upon it (عَلَيْهِ) there is a pause (وقْفٌ).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 97, verse 5:

﴿Peace it is﴾ (salam hiya): it is nothing but safety (salama), a predicate and subject. That is: Allah does not decree in it anything but safety and good, and He decrees in other nights affliction and safety. Or [the meaning is]: "It is nothing but peace (salam), because of how much the angels greet the believers" with peace. It was said: they do not meet a believing man or a believing woman without greeting them with peace on that night.

﴿Until the rising of the dawn﴾: that is, until the time of the dawn's rising. With a kasra on the lam (matla'i), it is read by ʿAlī and Khalaf. And those who disbelieved have been deprived of this peace.
